subject: physics
title: Circular Motion and Centripetal Force
welcome_lead: Round the bend with centripetal acceleration v²/r — and meet angular velocity along the way.
meta_desc: A-Level Further Mechanics adventure on circular motion and centripetal force.
final_note: Centripetal force always points to the centre — it changes direction, not speed.

concepts.def: v = ω r along the circular path.
F = m v² / r = m ω² r.
Time for one full revolution: T = 2π / ω.
Tilting a track so component of N provides force.

walkthroughs.body_html: ω is angle swept per second in radians. Full revolution = 2π rad, so ω = 2π / T = 2π f. Linear v = ω r.
Even at constant speed, direction changes, so there is acceleration a = v²/r = ω² r. This points to the centre of the circle.
F_c = m v²/r. The actual source varies: tension on a string, friction on a road, gravity in orbit, normal force on a banked curve.
